Netweb Technologies India.why: Indian OEM that designs and manufactures AI GPU systems (62% of Q1 FY27 revenue from AI systems, growing 484% YoY), so NVIDIA Blackwell-generation AI server demand from Indian sovereign AI, CSP and neocloud build-outs drives its revenue and order book.
Netweb Technologies India.evidence: Netweb Technologies India Q1 FY2027 (07-29-2026): CMD Sanjay Lodha: 'Our AI segment continues to be a key growth driver, contributing INR5,105.70 million, being 62% of revenue from operations'; 'all the solutions which we are selling like GB300, B300 and all, all are based on the latest architecture'.

players.product: Tyrone AI servers / supercomputing systems designed and manufactured in India: Camarero GB200 (NVIDIA GB200 NVL4), Camarero Spark (GB10), GB300 / B300-based AI solutions

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026) record quarter: revenue from operations INR8,197 million, up 172.1% YoY; operating EBITDA INR1,205 million, up 169%, margin 14.7%; PAT INR853 million, up 179.9%, PAT margin 10.3% (CMD Sanjay Lodha, CFO Ankit Kumar Singhal). AI segment contributed INR5,105.70 million, 62% of revenue from operations, growing 484% YoY; HPC INR1,252.94 million and Private Cloud INR1,353.46 million. CFO: ROCE 48.2%, ROE 44.6%; receivable days improved from 86 to 78 days; cash conversion cycle 96 days; net debt INR1,999 million as of June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue INR8,197 million (+172.1% YoY); AI segment INR5,105.70 million (62% of revenue, +484% YoY); PAT INR853 million (+179.9%)

quarterly_data.signal: Order book INR25,069.35 million as of June 30, 2026, with an L1 position (won, order not yet received) of INR8,480.47 million and a pipeline of INR104,100 million (CMD Sanjay Lodha). CMD: order book plus L1 is approximately INR3,400 crores; around 40% to 45% of the order book is on the AI side, the balance across HPC and private cloud. CFO Ankit Kumar Singhal: of the INR1,600 crores strategic order, close to INR430 crores was executed in the June quarter. CMD: 'there is no strategic order now. All orders are normal orders actually. The strategic is the new normal.' IR adviser Sanjeev Sancheti: the pipeline now includes the large AI orders previously reported separately as strategic (pipeline was INR4,400 crores without the strategic orders).
quarterly_data.figure: Order book INR25,069.35 million; L1 INR8,480.47 million; pipeline INR104,100 million; AI 40% to 45% of order book

quarterly_data.signal: CMD Sanjay Lodha's guidance: margins will remain between 13% to 14% (some basis points up or down); about 60% of the pipeline is expected to convert, over 18 to 24 months 'but not beyond that'; order-book execution is now guided at 16 to 20 weeks (earlier 8 to 12 weeks), 'it can stretch a little bit or can be early'. Existing facilities were built to sustain a turnover of INR3,000-plus crores, so no major capex is needed - only light and routine capex; the company does not guide revenue. CMD: worldwide AI compute demand is phenomenal and 'for at least for next 1.5 to 2 years, it will remain the same'.
quarterly_data.figure: Margin 13% to 14%; 60% pipeline conversion in 18 to 24 months; execution 16 to 20 weeks

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ankit Kumar Singhal: inventory days rose from 86 days in March to 110 days in June 2026, primarily from building raw-material stock 'to secure adequate inventory of key inputs in light of surging global demand for AI compute infrastructure'; given 'shortage shocks' across the industry the higher inventory is a deliberate decision, and he does not see memory prices softening in the next couple of quarters, 'maybe a year or so'. CMD Sanjay Lodha: component scarcity has been increasing over the last few quarters; direct relationships with technology providers and in-house manufacturing put Netweb 'in a better supply situation than others'; price increases are passed through on new orders and margins have not been impacted. CMD: 'more than the compute, the data center equipment is under shortage' - racks, chillers and other mechanical equipment.

CMD Sanjay Lodha on products: Netweb has stopped selling switches independently and uses current high-bandwidth switches inside its own solutions; 'all the solutions which we are selling like GB300, B300 and all, all are based on the latest architecture' and include those switches. CMD: Netweb is 'shipping the highest number of the large GPU deals' it is pursuing, does no box selling or contract manufacturing, and has an R&D team of around 125 people. Netweb has commenced R&D on quantum simulators and emulators and is investing in physical AI (focus on defense, national security and strategic manufacturing); no revenue guidance for these. CMD: exports are not a focus because domestic demand is phenomenal.

players.product: Tyrone AI servers / supercomputing systems designed and manufactured in India: Camarero GB200 (NVIDIA GB200 NVL4), Camarero Spark (GB10), GB300 / B300-based AI solutions

quarterly_data.signal: CMD Sanjay Lodha: India is seeing an unprecedented AI infrastructure build-out anchored by the India AI Mission GPU compute initiative, indigenous sovereign foundation models and demand from new cloud providers and CSPs; 'all the large cloud providers, everybody wants to come and set up data centers in India'. Chief Sales and Marketing Officer Hirdey Vikram: the pipeline covers both streams - CSPs and government on-prem procurement - and 'some of the largest players in the country' building Indian AI models use Netweb systems at the back end.
